knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Value of a Scalar

question.:question/problem:
If $kA=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -21 & 56\end{bmatrix}$,
where $A=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -3 & 8\end{bmatrix}$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To express $kA,$ we multiply each entry of $A$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kA & =k\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-1 & -3 & 8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}- k & - 3 k & 8 k\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}- k & - 3 k & 8 k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -21 & 56\end{bmatrix}
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the leftmost elements, $- k$ and $-7.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}- k & =-7 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

where $A=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -3 & 8\end{bmatrix}$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$

$$

$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kA$ in the problem statement:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}- k & - 3 k & 8 k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 & -21 & 56\end{bmatrix}
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the leftmost elements, $- k$ and $-7.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}- k & =-7 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

If $kB=\begin{bmatrix}33 & 36 \\ -12 & -24\end{bmatrix}$,
where $B=\begin{bmatrix}11 & 12 \\ -4 & -8\end{bmatrix}$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To express $kB,$ we multiply each entry of $B$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kB & =k\begin{bmatrix}11 & 12 \\ -4 & -8\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 k & 12 k \\ - 4 k & - 8 k\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kB$ in the problem statement:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}11 k & 12 k \\ - 4 k & - 8 k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}33 & 36 \\ -12 & -24\end{bmatrix}
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the elements in row $2$ and column $2$, $- 8 k$ and $-24.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}- 8 k & =-24 \\ k & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.

To express $kW,$ we multiply each entry of $W$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$

$$

$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the elements in row $2$ and column $2$, $4 k$ and $8.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4 k & =8 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

where $B=\begin{bmatrix}8 & -36 & 32\end{bmatrix}$
and $k$ is a scalar, calculate the value of $k.$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
To express $kB,$ we multiply each entry of $B$ by $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}kB & =k\begin{bmatrix}8 & -36 & 32\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}8 k & - 36 k & 32 k\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the above result equal to the matrix given for $kB$ in the problem statement:

$$
\begin{bmatrix}8 k & - 36 k & 32 k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -9 & 8\end{bmatrix}
$$

We can solve for $k$ by equating any two corresponding (nonzero) elements. Let's choose the rightmost elements, $32 k$ and $8.$ Equating these elements, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}32 k & =8 \\ k & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** We would still get the same result if we chose any other two corresponding (nonzero) elements.
